items.q: Persistent hoarseness beyond 3 weeks in a smoker mandates what?
items.exp: Early glottic cancer declares only by hoarseness while curable; three week persistence threshold triggers scope in guidelines, especially smokers and drinkers. Chronic laryngitis diagnosis also requires visualisation.
r: Incorrect. Inhalers do not exclude tumour.
items.kp: Three hoarse weeks in smoker: look at cords.

items.q: Glottic cancer enjoys best prognosis chiefly due to what two factors?
o: Early hoarseness presentation and sparse cord lymphatics delaying nodes
items.exp: True cords lack lymphatic drainage and voice change is immediate, so T1 glottic cures exceed 90 percent patterns with negligible nodal risk; supraglottic reverses both factors.
r: Correct. Early symptom plus poor lymphatics.
Incorrect. Patients are older smokers typically.
items.kp: Shouts early, spreads late: glottic luck.

items.q: Fixed vocal cord in laryngeal cancer signifies what staging implication?
o: Deep invasion (muscle, joint or cartilage spectrum) upstaging to at least T3 pattern
items.exp: Mobility loss means tumour invaded thyroarytenoid muscle, cricoarytenoid joint or beyond, defining advanced T categories and shifting toward combined modality or laryngectomy decisions.
r: Correct. Fixation equals deep invasion T3.
Incorrect. In cancer context fixation is invasion until proven.

items.q: Early T1 glottic carcinoma standard curative options preserving larynx are what?
o: Radiotherapy or transoral laser microsurgery (single modality)
items.exp: Both modalities cure similarly early; choice weighs voice quality, tumour exposure, patient preference, pulmonary status and salvage options in shared decision making.
r: Correct. Beam or laser, preserve larynx.
items.kp: Small cord cancer: laser or beam, keep box.

items.q: Organ preservation chemoradiation for advanced larynx means which strategy and caveat?
o: Concurrent cisplatin radiation preserving larynx in responders, salvage laryngectomy for persistence or recurrence; preserved but nonfunctional larynx may aspirate
items.exp: Landmark trials showed survival equivalence with larynx preservation in many, at cost of toxicity and need for salvage surgery readiness; function (swallow, airway) not just anatomy defines success.
r: Correct. Preserve responding organs, salvage failures.
items.kp: Save box if it still works; cut if cancer stays.

items.q: After total laryngectomy, most effective alaryngeal voice method in modern practice is what?
items.exp: One way valve prosthesis shunts pulmonary air to pharyngoesophageal segment producing fluent speech in most motivated patients; electrolarynx and oesophageal speech remain alternatives, stoma care education prevents water aspiration deaths.
r: Incorrect. Whisper lacks pulmonary drive post laryngectomy separation.
Incorrect. Larynx removal permanently separates airway.
items.kp: Valve in stoma gives new voice.

items.q: Supraglottic cancer node negative neck management differs from early glottic how?
o: Electively treat both neck sides (radiation or dissection) for supraglottic occult spread; early glottic neck usually observed
Neck surgery for glottic T1 mandatory
items.exp: Rich bilateral supraglottic lymphatics hide occult metastases in fifth to third of cases justifying elective treatment, while T1 glottic nodal risk is under few percent.
r: Correct. Elective bilateral neck for supraglottic.
Incorrect. Glottic T1 neck overtreatment avoided.
items.kp: Supraglottis drains rich: treat silent necks.

items.q: Impending airway obstruction from bulky laryngeal cancer safest securing method is what?
o: Awake tracheostomy under local anaesthesia (often planned before treatment)
items.exp: Distorted tumour anatomy defeats intubation and cricothyrotomy may cut tumour (bleeding, poor landmarks); awake tracheostomy with patient breathing, ENT present, is controlled standard, sometimes becoming permanent if laryngectomy follows.
r: Incorrect. Through tumour is last resort harm.
items.kp: Tumour airway: awake tracheostomy, no heroics.

items.q: Subglottic cancer rarity and presentation pattern is what?
o: Rarest subsite, late stridor and paratracheal spread, poorer prognosis
items.exp: Subglottic tumours (under 5 percent) grow silently in airway lumen until stridor, drain to paratracheal and mediastinal nodes, often needing laryngectomy with thyroid and node surgery.
r: Incorrect. Paediatric subglottic lesions are haemangioma or stenosis.

items.q: White patch on vocal cord (leukoplakia) management principle in persistent smoker lesion is what?
o: Biopsy or excisional stripping with histology for dysplasia grading and surveillance
items.exp: Cord leukoplakia spans hyperkeratosis to invasive cancer clinically indistinguishable; microlaryngoscopic excision grades dysplasia guiding surveillance or treatment, smoking cessation central. Thrush scrapes and context differs.
r: Incorrect. Persistent cord patch may be dysplasia.
Incorrect. Radiation needs cancer proof and staging.
items.kp: White cord patch earns microscope verdict.
